architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C46 provides evidence that the dual-axis modifier region can mitigate local thermal-hold instability under matched process and realization conditions.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Before physical adjudication, define success as replicate-level lower SI15–60 and SI15–90 for S1C46 than for the exact contemporaneous E2 control, with the direction reproduced in at least two independent realizations, neither S1C46 drift value reaching or exceeding the E5 reference values of 0.515 and 0.931, and no loss of measurable, interpretable viscosity response over 80–130 °C. If the effect is not reproducible or is smaller than the prespecified replicate uncertainty band, classify the result as unresolved rather than as mitigation.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the probe's mitigation claim if S1C46 has unchanged or higher hold drift than exact E2, either SI interval meets or exceeds the corresponding E5 reference without reproducible improvement, apparent benefit is only a static-viscosity shift, processability or temperature-response interpretation is lost, or stoichiometry/process-history matching is not verified.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 °C at 15, 60, and 90 min; calculate SI relative to the 15 min value; include the matched 80–130 °C temperature sweep and at least duplicate, preferably triplicate, independent realizations.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Full dual-axis coverage and lower modifier burden, but 15 wt% acrylic sufficiency is not locally established; retain as a lower-loading comparison only if resources permit.
Full dual-axis coverage and stronger coarse acrylic-region support, but its 25 wt% modifier burden is less conservative and less processability-focused than S1C46.
Useful only as a reactive-only control, but it is not the exact E2 reactive core and does not test the full performance-mitigation strategy.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The failure mode is thermal-hold instability, established locally by the large E5 drift relative to E1; static viscosity and temperature response are separate variables. The experiment intent is performance_mitigation, so both independently supported acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes must remain active. Local rheology shows a substantial realization/state shift and supports one-point scale calibration, while requiring direct 120 °C temporal hold measurement. Paper-derived rheological rules therefore determine the measurement and state-control design, not the candidate property. Curated PUR literature/database priors support the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like formulation families and a bounded coarse region, but do not predict the local wet-lab result or establish an optimum. S1C46 is selected as an uncertainty probe because it provides full dual-axis coverage and a higher-acrylic, 5 wt% tackifier comparison that addresses the Skeptic's objection that S1C41 was promoted by minimum burden before sufficiency was demonstrated. Minimum sufficient intervention is therefore not used as the primary reason for selection. The Robustness Adjudicator's objections are resolved by requiring an exact contemporaneous E2 control, verified modifier functionality and final NCO:OH, matched process history, replicate-level adjudication, and preservation of the 120 °C hold endpoint. The probe should not be interpreted as an exact-property prediction or as proof that the external analogue region is locally optimal.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required first to establish the supported formulation-versus-state response structure, determine whether state calibration materially improves the model, distinguish thermal response from temporal hold drift, and obtain the paper-derived measurement implications before candidate comparison.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective is established, obtain the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, retain the original E2 reactive-core anchor, and identify independently supported acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes without treating the hypothesis as a discovered optimum.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Characterize the measured original reactive-core reference and its composition fractions before judging modifier changes, while keeping composition effects separate from the large observed realization/process-state spread.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Use source-level curated evidence only after the local failure mode is established, to verify chemically plausible acrylic and minor-tackifier intervention regions and their limitations; do not use it to declare an optimum or to import an exact hold-stability threshold.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold stability: SI from 15 to 60 min and 15 to 90 min at 120 °C, using absolute SI for loss evaluation.
Initial and time-resolved viscosity level within measured temperature and time support, preserving unknown source units.
Temperature-response shape over 80–130 °C and consistency with the state-aware model after any required one-point calibration.
Repeatability across independent runs and, where feasible, retest after controlled storage or process-history handling.
Sensitivity to realization/process state, including whether state calibration reduces apparent candidate differences.
Reactive-core and stoichiometric feasibility relative to E2.
Acrylic-like modifier fraction and modifier functionality as separate design variables where supported.
Minor tackifier-like fraction, bounded conservatively at or below the evidence-supported coarse region.
Extrapolation distance from directly measured local compositions, temperatures, and hold times.
Evidence quality: directly commensurate local measurement versus directional or noncommensurate external analogue evidence.
counterfactual_checks: Would the proposed intervention still be preferred if all candidates were compared after the same one-point state calibration?
Would the decision change if the observed E2 repeat spread were treated as a process-state uncertainty band rather than random measurement noise?
Is the apparent improvement in hold stability still present after matching initial viscosity level and temperature-response support?
Could the result be explained by altered reactive-core or MDI stoichiometry rather than the intended modifier axis?
Would a single-axis modifier change be preferable if the stated objective were causal isolation instead of performance mitigation?
Does the candidate remain feasible if the external 15–25 wt% acrylic anchors are treated only as directional evidence rather than exact targets?
Does the candidate outperform the local E1/E5 hold contrast without relying on a literature time scale or stability threshold outside the measured 15–90 min window?
If hold drift is unchanged but viscosity level improves, does the candidate fail the primary mitigation objective?
If hold drift improves but repeatability remains comparable to E2, is the result robust enough for advancement or does it require an uncertainty-resolution experiment?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate experiment that mitigates the established thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure while preserving measurable processability and remaining within the original E2 reactive-core and evidence-supported modifier space.
design_implications: Do not optimize only a nominal viscosity value; adjudication must include thermal-hold drift at the measured 120 °C condition and the measured 15–90 min window.
Use the state-aware rheology findings to decide whether the candidate must receive one-point state calibration before comparing viscosity or temperature-response behavior.
Preserve the measured temperature support of 80–130 °C and avoid claims outside that range unless explicitly identified as extrapolation.

Because the failure mode is established, a bounded multi-component intervention is admissible in performance_mitigation mode when each modifier axis is independently supported; single-axis isolation is not mandatory.
Keep reactive-core identity, stoichiometric balance, modifier loading, process history, and realization state explicit so chemistry effects are not conflated with state effects.
Treat acrylic anchors near 15–20 wt% and tackifier guidance below about 10 wt% as coarse evidence-supported regions only; do not convert them into an exact optimum.

Use directly commensurate local E1/E5 hold trajectories for the primary stability decision, directional external comparisons for intervention-family selection, and conservative bounded-region principles to limit extrapolation.
material_regularities_to_use: The measured temperature sweeps are monotonic decreasing with temperature over 80–130 °C for E1, E2, and E3, so viscosity level and temperature response are distinct from thermal-hold drift.

E2 shows substantial nominal repeat spread across three runs, with CV approximately 0.46–0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8–3.6; a single nominal viscosity should not be treated as a fully repeatable material property.
E1 and E5 provide a direct local contrast in thermal-hold behavior at 120 °C, establishing hold drift as an actionable design objective rather than merely a temperature-response effect.

Run-to-run and retest structure indicate that realization history or state calibration may contribute to observed rheology; the state-shift master-curve result must determine how strongly state calibration is required.

The external evidence supports acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like intervention axes, but the reported percentages are noncommensurate analogues or directional guidance rather than exact local optima.
The candidate lattice is bounded by the pre-result evidence: acrylic-like modifier levels from 0 to 30 wt% and tackifier-like levels from 0 to 10 wt%, with E2 retained as the reactive-core anchor.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold instability is the primary failure mode: the original E5 profile shows large viscosity drift at 120 °C (SI 0.515 from 15 to 60 min and 0.931 from 15 to 90 min), whereas E1 is comparatively stable (SI 0.095 and 0.168). This must be separated from viscosity level, temperature response, and realization/process-state uncertainty.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep over the measured 80–130 °C range with the same protocol and replicate structure used for the original measurements.
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 °C at minimum at 15, 60, and 90 min, with SI calculated relative to the 15 min value.
At least duplicate, preferably triplicate, runs to quantify realization and repeatability risk rather than relying on one nominal curve.
Explicit recording of material age, preconditioning, thermal history, mixing sequence, shear or equilibration history, and measurement order.
One-point state calibration if the state-aware summary shows a meaningful state shift or calibration benefit.
Initial viscosity level and temperature-response descriptors reported separately from hold-stability descriptors.
Composition verification of reactive core, acrylic-like modifier, tackifier-like modifier, and MDI fractions, including stoichiometric quantities and any uncertain values.
Adjudication against the frozen pre-result objective and weights, without rewriting criteria after observing the result.
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary shows a substantial state shift or materially better state-aware than formulation-only prediction.
Candidate performance differences are smaller than the observed E2 repeat spread.
The candidate is outside directly measured composition, temperature, or time support.
A modifier changes viscosity level but hold drift is not measured over the local window.
Acrylic functionality, tackifier identity, MDI level, or stoichiometric balance differs simultaneously, preventing a clear interpretation.
The candidate approaches the upper acrylic or tackifier lattice bounds based only on directional literature evidence.
Process history or thermal preconditioning is not matched across candidates.
The candidate has insufficient replicate coverage or an anomalous single run.
External evidence reports viscosity at a different temperature, unit, time window, or chemistry and is being used as if directly commensurate.
Observed improvement in hold stability is accompanied by unsupported extrapolation in viscosity or temperature response.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The selected modifier formulation mitigates the local thermal-hold instability rather than merely changing nominal viscosity.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Pass provisionally only if, relative to a matched contemporaneous E2 reactive-only control, the candidate shows lower SI15–60 and SI15–90 with replicate-consistent direction, and both drift values remain below the E5 failure reference of 0.515 and 0.931 respectively; initial viscosity and the 80–130 °C response must remain measurable and interpretable.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the primary mitigation claim if hold drift is unchanged or higher than the matched E2 control, if either hold interval meets or exceeds the E5 failure reference without a reproducible improvement, or if apparent improvement is observed only as a static viscosity shift without reduced hold drift.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 °C, 15–90 min, with SI referenced to 15 min and replicate-level reporting.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at 120 °C, with SI calculated relative to the 15 min value at 15, 60, and 90 min; report SI15–60 and SI15–90 separately from initial viscosity and the 80–130 °C temperature-response curve.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Match material age, preconditioning, thermal history, mixing sequence, shear/equilibration history, and measurement order across candidates. If the state-aware shift remains relevant, use one in-range viscosity anchor at 120 °C for each realization before comparing temperature-response shape; do not use the anchor as a substitute for the hold test.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: Measure at 15, 60, and 90 min at 120 °C, with the same 80–130 °C temperature-sweep protocol before or after the hold as used for the local reference measurements; use at least duplicate and preferably triplicate independent realizations.

Whether the 15 wt% acrylic level is sufficient, or whether the system requires the higher acrylic region represented by S1C46 or S1C51.
Whether modifier functionality and true reactive stoichiometry alter the result.

Strong analogue-region support and preserved E2 reactive-core identity.

Whether improved drift is independent of an altered initial viscosity level.
Whether the higher modifier burden compromises processability within the measured 80–130 °C support.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It is a matched-axis robustness point that tests whether the rank-1 result is sensitive to modest acrylic loading. Its value is not closeness to a literature percentage; it is the interpretable contrast with S1C41 under the same tackifier level and controlled state.

evidence_against: The 25 wt% total modifier burden is larger than S1C41 and S1C46, so it is not preferred by minimum sufficient intervention.

A literature viscosity value at 120 °C is not a thermal-hold stability measurement and cannot substitute for the local hold trajectory.
evidence_for: Full intervention coverage with 20 wt% acrylic-like modifier and 5 wt% tackifier-like modifier.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 shows severe 120 °C viscosity drift, with SI of 0.515 from 15–60 min and 0.931 from 15–90 min, while E1 is comparatively stable at 0.095 and 0.168.
Measured local evidence: E1/E5 hold trajectories demonstrate that thermal-hold drift is formulation-dependent and distinct from static viscosity and temperature response.
Measured local evidence: E2 has substantial repeat spread, with CV approximately 0.46–0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8–3.6.

Derived model rule: realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a shared temperature-response shape remains transferable; state-aware R2 is 0.9977 versus 0.8519 for the formulation-only model.
Derived measurement rule: one in-range state-specific anchor can calibrate the local thermal-response shape with approximately 6–10% pooled multiplicative error.

External analogue evidence, directly commensurate only in coarse formulation terms: acrylic-like resin examples near 19–20 wt% and a 25 wt% low-OH acrylic example support an acrylic intervention region, but not an exact local optimum.

External analogue evidence, directional/noncommensurate: tackifier-containing PUR examples near 4.8–6.4 wt% and guidance below about 10 wt% support a minor-tackifier family and coarse region, without proving local hold stability.
Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, both independently supported modifier axes should be covered before using minimum sufficient total modifier burden as a tie-break.
Unresolved uncertainty: acrylic functionality, modifier identity, process history, and realization state may affect hold drift independently of nominal composition.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate thermal-hold viscosity drift at 120 °C while preserving processability and the E2 reactive-core proportions, using a directly measured 15–90 min hold assessment and explicit control of realization/process state.
unresolved_questions: Does the combined acrylic-like/tackifier-like intervention reduce local hold drift after state calibration and matched initial-condition handling?
Is S1C41 sufficient, or is a higher acrylic loading such as S1C46 or S1C51 required?
What is the contribution of modifier functionality and verified reactive-group content to hold stability?
Can candidate differences be distinguished from the large E2 realization/process-state spread?
Does any hold-drift improvement persist without unacceptable changes in initial viscosity or temperature-response shape?
The evidence supports a family and bounded region, not an exact optimum composition; exact loading should remain unresolved until matched local hold measurements are obtained.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Retains full dual-axis coverage and the same 5 wt% tackifier level while increasing acrylic to 17.5 wt%; it has stronger regional support than S1C41 but a higher 22.5 wt% modifier burden.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The objective remains performance mitigation and the experiment must test a more defensible acrylic region before declaring the lower loading sufficient.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Provides full coverage and a stronger analogue-supported acrylic level, but uses a larger 25 wt% total modifier burden and is less conservative for processability.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: Directly commensurate approximately 20 wt% acrylic-region evidence is prioritized over minimizing modifier burden.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Lowest-burden full-coverage candidate, but currently an uncertainty-resolution point rather than a justified performance rank-1.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A higher-acrylic comparison has already established that the intervention family is sufficient and the remaining question is whether burden can be reduced.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Cleaner control role, but the supplied S1C01 composition is not the exact E2 formulation and does not test the dual-axis mitigation strategy.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A corrected exact-E2 reactive-only control is constructed for causal or state-matched comparison.

required_conditions: Include an exact contemporaneous E2 reactive-only control using the verified original E2 core fractions and recalculated reactive stoichiometry.
Verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality and recalculate final NCO:OH for the selected modifier formulation and control.
Treat S1C41 as a lower-loading uncertainty point rather than rank-1 unless tested alongside a higher-acrylic full-coverage point such as S1C46.
Prespecify replicate-level effect-size, uncertainty-overlap, and anomalous-run handling rules relative to exact E2.
Match and record material age, preconditioning, thermal history, mixing, equilibration or shear history, and measurement order.
Use one-point state calibration only for viscosity-scale or temperature-response interpretation; retain the 120 °C temporal trajectory as the primary stability endpoint.
Do not interpret external analogue percentages as local sufficiency, mechanism, or optimum loading.
Resolve the historical provenance of the candidate grid and ranking implementation before making a fully prospective claim.

robustness_checks.detail: The proposal directly targets the established 120 °C thermal-hold viscosity drift and measures SI15–60 and SI15–90 over the locally supported 15–90 min window.
The Planner declares performance_mitigation, for which a dual-axis intervention is appropriate because acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes are independently supported.
S1C41 covers both supported intervention axes; its rank is not based on sacrificing axis coverage.

robustness_checks.check: Robustness to removal of exact analogue-distance rewards
robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 remains inside the supported bounded region, but its rank-1 status is not stable once exact analogue distance is treated only as regional evidence. S1C46 and S1C51 have comparable full coverage and stronger direct acrylic-region support.

S1C41 is promoted largely because of lower modifier burden before sufficiency of 15 wt% acrylic has been demonstrated locally. Burden is a valid tie-break only after intervention sufficiency is established.

The proposed S1C01 control is not the exact E2 reactive core: its MDI and core fractions differ. High process-history uncertainty and unresolved modifier functionality or reactive stoichiometry further limit composition-only interpretation.

The proposed temperature sweep, 120 °C hold trajectory, replication, and state anchoring are appropriate, but the acceptance rule lacks a prespecified quantitative effect-size and uncertainty criterion relative to an exact contemporaneous E2 control.

The recommendation depends on unverified final NCO:OH balance, assumed sufficiency of the lower acrylic loading, and an imperfect control formulation. State calibration cannot substitute for measuring temporal hold drift.

counterfactual_failures: If all candidates are compared after state calibration, S1C41 may not remain preferable because its lower burden is not evidence that its hold-drift mitigation is sufficient.
If E2 repeat spread is treated as a process-state uncertainty band, the proposal does not specify the minimum effect needed to distinguish S1C41 from state variation.
If initial viscosity is matched, the proposal does not establish whether the acrylic/tackifier combination retains a hold-drift advantage.
The proposal cannot determine whether a higher acrylic point such as S1C46 or S1C51 is required without testing or explicitly treating S1C41 as an uncertainty probe rather than a performance rank-1.
The E5 threshold comparison is local and appropriate as a reference, but it does not replace a prespecified effect-size criterion relative to the contemporaneous exact-E2 control.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 is ranked first primarily because 15 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier has lower total burden than S1C46 and S1C51. No local hold data establish that 15 wt% acrylic is sufficient to mitigate drift. S1C46 and S1C51 have the same full intervention coverage and comparable interpretability, while their acrylic levels have stronger direct analogue support.
critical_findings.issue: Minimum sufficient intervention is applied before intervention sufficiency has been demonstrated.

critical_findings.evidence: Original E2 has MDI fraction 0.2019067, whereas S1C01 has MDI fraction 0.1928667 and different PDP70/PPG2000 fractions. Therefore, comparison to S1C01 cannot be described as a matched contemporaneous E2 reactive-only control without explicitly accepting a reactive-core or stoichiometric difference.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed matched E2 control is not actually the original E2 reactive-core composition.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis states that AC1920 or TK100 may contribute reactive groups and that true NCO:OH must be recalculated from verified specifications. The proposal preserves relative E2 core proportions but does not establish the final reactive balance after adding S1C41 modifiers.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive stoichiometry remains unresolved for both modifier axes.

critical_findings.evidence: Terms such as 'replicate-consistent direction,' 'measurable,' and 'interpretable' are not assigned a prespecified replicate-level rule, effect-size margin, uncertainty criterion, or handling rule for overlapping results. Given the E2 CV of approximately 0.46–0.58, a small directional difference may be indistinguishable from realization-state variation.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criterion is not sufficiently quantitative for adjudication.

critical_findings.evidence: H08 is explicitly noncommensurate and its denominator is not fully verified. The directly commensurate acrylic analogue cluster is approximately 19–20 wt%, while 15 wt% is retained as a directional lower-region point rather than an exact total-formulation anchor.
critical_findings.issue: The 15 wt% acrylic basis is weaker than the proposal's wording suggests.

critical_findings.evidence: The tackifier and acrylic families are independently supported by external analogues, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the combination reduces local hold drift or that either axis remains effective after matching initial viscosity and state.
critical_findings.issue: Independent support exists for each modifier axis, but not for the combined intervention or its interaction.

critical_findings.evidence: All scorecards report six missing process-history fields and high process-history uncertainty. Matching history prospectively is useful, but the candidate cannot be interpreted as a composition-only intervention unless age, preconditioning, mixing, equilibration, shear, and measurement order are recorded and controlled.
critical_findings.issue: Process-history uncertainty is acknowledged but not resolved in the candidate definition.

interpretability_failures: S1C41 versus S1C01 does not isolate modifier effects because S1C01 is not the exact original E2 reactive core.
Any apparent improvement could reflect altered effective NCO:OH balance, modifier functionality, initial viscosity, or realization state rather than the intended acrylic/tackifier intervention.
A one-point 120 °C state anchor calibrates viscosity scale and temperature-response shape but does not identify or remove temporal hold drift.
The proposed pass/fail language lacks a prespecified quantitative rule for replicate consistency and for differences smaller than the E2 repeat spread.

leakage_check.detail: No validation formulation identity, wet-lab outcome, or outcome-derived label is visible, and the proposal explicitly states that these were excluded. However, the payload also states that the current exact V2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. This leaves historical provenance of the operational candidate grid and ranking rule unresolved, although direct result leakage is not demonstrated.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly targets the measured 120 °C thermal-hold drift, requires full coverage of both independently supported modifier axes for performance mitigation, separates hold drift from static viscosity and temperature response, and incorporates state-aware calibration. However, rank-1 selection relies on minimum modifier burden before intervention sufficiency is established, and the stated E2 control is not compositionally identical to the original E2 anchor.

required_corrections: Include an exact contemporaneous E2 reactive-only control using the original E2 core fractions and verified reactive stoichiometry; do not substitute S1C01 unless its composition is explicitly corrected and justified.
Verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality and recalculate the final NCO:OH balance for S1C41, S1C46, and any other performance candidate.

Do not call S1C41 rank-1 on minimum burden until intervention sufficiency is established. Either test S1C41 together with a higher-acrylic full-coverage point such as S1C46, or relabel S1C41 as an uncertainty-resolution point.
Predefine a quantitative replicate adjudication rule, including the required effect relative to exact E2, treatment of overlapping uncertainty, and handling of anomalous runs.
Require the state anchor only as a scale/shape calibration and retain the 120 °C 15–90 min trajectory as the primary stability measurement.
Record and match material age, preconditioning, thermal history, mixing sequence, equilibration/shear history, and measurement order across exact E2 and modifier candidates.
Preserve the distinction that external 15–20 wt% acrylic and approximately 5 wt% tackifier values support bounded candidate generation only, not local sufficiency, mechanism, or optimum loading.
Resolve the historical provenance of the candidate grid and ranking implementation before treating the recommendation as a fully prospective frozen decision.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundary between local measured evidence and external analogue evidence, and does not treat literature percentages or static viscosity as local hold-stability evidence. It nevertheless presents S1C41 as the minimum practically sufficient performance candidate without local evidence of sufficiency, and it describes comparison against a matched E2 control that is not the exact E2 composition.

tool_trace.reason: Required first to establish the supported formulation-versus-state response structure, determine whether state calibration materially improves the model, distinguish thermal response from temporal hold drift, and obtain the paper-derived measurement implications before candidate comparison.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
